name: MuSR
intro: MuSR 是面向自然长叙事中多步软推理的英文基准。论文以领域模板、黄金事实 F 与多样性事实 G、GPT-4 递归推理树和领域专属故事实现构建 564 篇叙事与 756 道问题；谋杀谜案和物体放置使用树校验器与章节化，团队分配不使用这两项机制。
build_method: 神经符号生成, 自动生成, 人工验证, 混合
eval_feature: 递归推理树, 领域专属叙事生成, 端到端可解性验证, 思维链与神经符号评测
build_method_en: Neurosymbolic Generation, Automated Generation, Human Validation, Hybrid
eval_feature_en: Recursive Reasoning Trees, Domain-specific Narrative Generation, End-to-end Solvability Validation, CoT and Neurosymbolic Evaluation
intro_en: MuSR is an English benchmark for multistep soft reasoning in long natural narratives. Its paper builds 564 narratives and 756 questions from domain templates, gold facts F, diversity facts G, GPT-4 recursive reasoning trees, and domain-specific story realization; murder mystery and object placement use tree validators and chaptering, while team allocation uses neither.

drawio_review_note: Evidence freeze [site-a11w-source-only]: paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.16049v2 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2310.16049v2, downloaded PDF SHA-256 ba92c00a0179abacd65cbae2de4254c41cf3dd82d82d26ec02e4ee8be054265f and arXiv v2 source-tar SHA-256 f76a0afc756d10a45f65bdf109d817add9087f57ed861a8ab536012024677aca; official repository https://github.com/Zayne-sprague/MuSR/tree/b1f4d4168a9cfc6760e8b74d728e4516023dfaa5 at commit b1f4d4168a9cfc6760e8b74d728e4516023dfaa5 dated 2024-08-10. Repository evidence hashes are LICENSE 2c8e2a28ca013557c73dff03ab3055b76f226dbeb8daa20dc36caeefe76f7946, README c0061c7245e572967920df9bc35fe5e6223134299d9aadd01de20f42cffd1440, and eval/eval.py 07f325490cd2ae5d0ed773b1b5df99930aa5bab28ea8560835982e75607d4878. Released JSON hashes are murder_mystery.json 2d21b133c3ab2c0cf8d58cf5c0d8f9b269e1451b4ba6d3a639872e12203fdf63, object_placements.json db3789d265b9869811d967770873c1397634be53093d8a46ba1a92be1a3292f1, and team_allocation.json f25653d60abf4e93ecf368e1a83be321cb400df41e43fe7fadc76b023c4b56c1. Paper locators: Section 3 and Figure 2 (PDF page 4) define the three stages, tuples (F,T,x,{q},{a}), hidden-at-test F/T, and the F/G contract; Sections 3.2–3.3 (PDF pages 4–5) define recursive GPT-4 completion, S(T)/C(T), domain validators, up-to-three retries followed by pruning, and chaptering. Sections 4.1–4.3 (PDF pages 5–6) define Murder Mystery, Object Placements, and Team Allocation. Section 5.1 and Tables 2–4 (PDF pages 7–8) give dataset sizes, rule baselines, seven-person triple annotation, majority scores, creation ablations, and the explicit statement that Team Allocation did not require chaptering or validators. Section 5.2 and Tables 5–7 (PDF pages 8–9) define zero-shot CoT+ main results, Regular/CoT/CoT+/1-shot/Few-shot prompt variants, the three-example few-shot limit, and Decomposed Prompting, SymbolicTOM, and PAL as domain-specific methods. Appendix G.1 Algorithm 1 (PDF page 32) specifies recursive expansion. Appendix H.1 and Table 9 (PDF pages 51–52) specify GPT-4 for all creation prompts, temperature/top-p 1.0, paper maximum depths 4/3/2, and evaluation setup; Appendix I gives CoT+ and PAL prompts. The diagram preserves domain facts: Murder has two suspects and means/motive/opportunity; Object has three people, three moves, two items and p=0.33 observation; Team has three people, two tasks, 0/1/2 skill/teamwork scores and a best-vs-runner-up margin of at least two. It separates Murder/Object validators and chaptered story paths from Team's one-pass story path. The official files contain 250 Murder narratives/questions, 64 Object narratives carrying four questions each (256 questions), and 250 Team narratives/questions: 564 narratives and 756 questions total. Quality validation is represented only as disclosed: rule baselines 50.0/35.9/none and triple annotation of 34/40/34 instances by seven annotators with majority 94.1/95.0/100.0. The paper explicitly does not formally evaluate fluency, coherence, or intrinsic commonsense sensibility, so the diagram does not claim those as passed release gates. Fixed-code audit: all three creator scripts seed random with 0; current scripts default to depths 3/3/2, so Murder differs from paper depth 4; Murder/Object use validators and three structure retries, while Team uses one structure retry and says chaptering is unnecessary. Released eval/eval.py currently configures CoT+ and gpt-4 by default, uses temperature/top-p 1.0, max_tokens 2400, takes the last nonempty lowercase answer: line, accepts the gold digit anywhere or the first present choice digit, randomly samples a choice when no valid digit appears, optionally majority-votes repeated samples, and reports correct/total Accuracy. It asks for murder_mysteries.json, but the repository releases murder_mystery.json, so the unchanged fixed script cannot run all three released domains. Openness boundary: the repository root carries MIT, but released JSON rows have no embedded dataset-specific license/provenance field; the repository has no tags or GitHub releases and supplies no author checksums. Its HTML viewer accepts local dataset uploads and answers, not benchmark-result submissions; no formal leaderboard submission workflow was found, so has_leaderboard is false. This A11w revision intentionally updates bilingual specs and page metadata only; formal Draw.io, architecture, SVG, PNG, and manifest assets remain untouched pending the formal publication phase. Formal publication evidence [site-a11w-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 5405×1265 (English) and 5405×1265 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 5403×1263 and 5403×1263. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
